chapters.title: Chapter 1: What the Forex Market Is

lessons.title: What Is Forex? The World's Largest Market Explained Simply

children.text: Tanvi, a 24-year-old analyst in Pune, signs up for a US online certification that costs $2,000. When her card statement arrives, the charge is not $2,000. It is ₹1,91,000. Nobody at her bank picked that number at random. It came from the foreign exchange market, and that same market decides what you pay for petrol, an iPhone, a Dubai holiday and every US stock you buy through an LRS app. By the end of this lesson you will know what forex is, how big it is, where it actually trades, and the one legal line every Indian resident must not cross.

body.text: A currency has no price of its own. Its price is always quoted in another currency, so every forex trade is buying one currency and selling another at the same moment.

children.text: What Forex Actually Is

markDefs.definition: The price of one currency expressed in another. USD/INR at 95.50 means 1 US dollar costs ₹95.50.
Two currencies quoted together, such as USD/INR or EUR/USD. The first is the base currency, the second is the quote currency.

children.text: Forex, short for foreign exchange and also called FX, is the global market where currencies are swapped for one another. The price at which one currency swaps for another is the
exchange rate
, and because you always need two currencies to express a price, forex is quoted in a
currency pair
. When a news anchor says "the rupee closed at 95.54," they mean the USD/INR pair: one US dollar cost ₹95.54.

Compare that with a share. Reliance Industries has a price in rupees on NSE. The rupee itself has no price in rupees. It only has a price in dollars, euros, dirhams or yen. That is why "the rupee fell" and "the dollar rose" describe exactly the same event.
You Already Use Forex Every Week
At the petrol pump.
India imports most of its crude oil and pays for it in dollars. A weaker rupee makes every barrel costlier for Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL.
In electronics prices.
Phones, laptops and their components are largely priced in dollars. When USD/INR rises, launch prices in India tend to follow.
In your US stock portfolio.
If you own Apple or an S&P 500 ETF through an LRS platform, your return in rupees depends on the stock and on USD/INR.
In family remittances.
A son in Dubai sending AED 5,000 home to Kerala is doing a forex conversion. The exchange rate decides how many rupees his parents receive.
Worked Example: Why the Rate Matters

body.caption: Converting a dollar amount into rupees
Tanvi's $2,000 course fee at two different exchange rates

children.text: The course did not get more expensive. The rupee got cheaper. A 5.50 move in USD/INR, about 6%, added ₹11,000 to Tanvi's bill without the US institute changing a single thing.

body.title: The freelancer's invoice
body.prompt: Arjun, a freelance designer in Jaipur, invoices a US client $5,000. On the day he raised the invoice, USD/INR was 95.50. By the time the money arrives, USD/INR is 92.00. How many fewer rupees does Arjun receive because of the rate change?
body.explanation: At 95.50, $5,000 × 95.50 = ₹4,77,500. At 92.00, $5,000 × 92.00 = ₹4,60,000. The difference is ₹17,500. A stronger rupee hurts anyone who earns in dollars, which is exactly why exporters and IT companies watch USD/INR closely.

children.text: Put those numbers side by side. At a USD/INR rate of 95.50, NSE's ₹1.2 lakh crore of daily cash turnover is roughly $12.6 billion. Global forex trades about $9.6 trillion a day, more than 750 times as much. No stock exchange, bond market or commodity market in the world comes close.

body.text: Why does the dollar show up in 89.2% of trades? Because it is the world's middle currency. A Tiruppur exporter selling to Brazil is usually invoiced in dollars, not in rupees or reais. Even trades between two non-dollar currencies often route through the dollar because that is where the deepest liquidity sits.

children.text: Where Does Forex Actually Trade?

markDefs.definition: Over-the-counter. Trades negotiated directly between two parties, usually banks, rather than matched on a central exchange.

children.text: When you buy HDFC Bank shares on Zerodha, your order goes to NSE or BSE, gets matched against a seller, and settles through a clearing corporation. Most forex does not work like that. The bulk of global currency trading is
OTC
: big banks quote prices to each other and to clients over electronic networks, and there is no single building or exchange where "the" price is set.

columns.label: Stock market (NSE, BSE)
points: Central exchange matches every buy and sell order

You own a share in a company

Slightly different prices from different dealers

You swap one currency for another

body.title: Why forex runs 24 hours: the global sessions in IST

children.text: Forex follows the sun. As one financial centre winds down, the next one opens, so global dealing never fully stops on weekdays. Approximate main trading windows in Indian time:

content.caption: Major forex sessions in IST (approximate, during Northern Hemisphere summer)

cells: Week opens here on Monday morning
Largest centre; overlaps with India's afternoon
US data releases often land around 6:00 pm IST

children.text: When the UK and US move their clocks back for winter, the London and New York windows shift about one hour later in IST. India's own onshore rupee market and NSE's currency derivatives segment run from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm IST, which is why big US news that breaks at night usually shows up as a gap in USD/INR the next morning.

body.title: Exchange or not?
body.question: Which statement about the global forex market is correct?
options: All currency trades are matched on one central exchange in London
Most forex trades happen over the counter between banks and their clients
Forex trades only between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm IST
SEBI sets the USD/INR exchange rate every morning
body.explanation: Forex is mostly OTC. London is the largest trading centre, not a central exchange. The market runs around the clock on weekdays, and SEBI does not set the rupee's price. The rate is set by trading, with RBI stepping in to smooth sharp moves.

Key Moments in the Rupee's Forex History

events.title: Balance of payments crisis
events.description: With reserves barely enough for a few weeks of imports, RBI devalues the rupee in two steps by roughly 18 to 19%.

events.title: Market-determined exchange rate
events.description: India moves to a unified, market-determined rate. Supply and demand, not a fixed official rate, now set the rupee's price.

events.title: FEMA replaces FERA
events.description: The Foreign Exchange Management Act shifts forex law from criminal control to civil management. It still governs how residents can deal in foreign currency.

events.title: NSE launches USD/INR futures
events.description: Retail investors get a regulated, exchange-traded way to take positions on the rupee.

events.title: Taper tantrum
events.description: Fears of the US Fed pulling back stimulus trigger foreign outflows. The rupee hits a then record low of about 68.85.

events.title: RBI Alert List launched
events.description: RBI starts publishing names of unauthorised forex trading platforms targeting Indian residents.

events.title: Rupee near 95.5
events.description: Elevated crude prices, global risk aversion and foreign outflows keep the rupee under pressure, even as India's forex reserves hit a record $785.7 billion in the week ended 4 September.

body.text: A falling rupee is not simply "bad news." It hurts importers, oil marketing companies and students paying foreign fees. It helps exporters and companies that earn in dollars, such as TCS and Infosys. Whether a currency move is good or bad always depends on which side of the trade you are on.

children.text: Using Forex vs Trading Forex: The Legal Line

Buying dollars for a trip, paying a foreign university or sending money abroad under LRS is using forex for a genuine purpose, done through a bank or authorised dealer. Trading forex means taking positions to profit from rate moves. For Indian residents, that second activity is tightly restricted, and this is where most beginners get into trouble.

body.label: Legal ways for an Indian resident to deal in currencies
body.value: Authorised banks for genuine needs, and recognised exchanges such as NSE and BSE
body.context: Rupee-pair derivatives like USD/INR may be used only to hedge a genuine currency exposure. Cross-currency contracts such as EUR/USD on Indian exchanges can be traded within exchange limits. Offshore leveraged forex apps are not a legal route. Chapter 4 covers the rules in detail.

body.text: If an Instagram ad, Telegram group or "forex mentor" asks you to deposit money through UPI into an app offering 1:500 leverage on EUR/USD or gold, stop. Remitting money abroad to trade forex on margin is not permitted under FEMA, and RBI's Alert List named 95 unauthorised platforms and promoters as of its November 2025 update. RBI also says the list is not exhaustive, so a name missing from it does not mean the platform is authorised.

body.label: RBI: Alert List of Unauthorised Forex Trading Platforms
body.description: Check any forex app, website or "trading academy" against RBI's official Alert List before sharing KYC details or money.

body.title: The Telegram tip
body.scenario: Meera, a 29-year-old teacher in Lucknow, joins a Telegram group called "Forex Freedom India." The admin posts screenshots of ₹40,000 daily profits on EUR/USD and gold, and says: "Open an account on our partner app, deposit just ₹10,000 by UPI, get 1:500 leverage. Totally legal, lakhs of Indians do it."
body.prompt: Based on this lesson, what should Meera recognise about this offer, and what should she do instead if she genuinely wants exposure to currency moves?
body.modelAnswer:
1. "Lakhs of Indians do it" does not make it legal. For residents, currency dealing must go through authorised banks or recognised Indian exchanges such as NSE and BSE, never an offshore app.
2. Depositing money to trade forex on margin with an offshore platform breaches FEMA, and UPI collection by such apps is a common pattern in RBI's warnings.
3. 1:500 leverage means a 0.2% move against her can wipe out her entire deposit. Profit screenshots are easy to fake and say nothing about losses.
4. She should search the app and its promoters on RBI's Alert List, and remember the list is not exhaustive.
5. If she wants to learn currency trading, she should first finish learning how quotes, leverage and margin work. On Indian exchanges, rupee pairs like USD/INR may be used only to hedge a genuine currency exposure, which she does not have, but cross-currency contracts such as EUR/USD can be traded through a SEBI-registered broker within exchange limits.

body.title: The core idea
body.textWithBlank: Every forex trade involves buying one currency and ___ another at the same time.
body.explanation: A currency only has a price in terms of another currency, so every trade is two-sided. Buying USD/INR means buying dollars and selling rupees.

cards.definition: The global market where one currency is exchanged for another.
The price of one currency in terms of another, such as ₹95.50 per US dollar.
Two currencies quoted together, like USD/INR. The first is the base, the second is the quote.
A market where trades are negotiated directly between parties, usually banks, instead of on a central exchange.
The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, which governs how Indian residents can deal in foreign exchange.
RBI's published list of unauthorised forex trading platforms and their promoters. It is not exhaustive.

points: Forex is the market for swapping one currency for another, and every price is quoted as a currency pair such as USD/INR.
Exchange rates affect you directly through fuel, electronics, foreign fees, remittances and US investments.
At about $9.6 trillion a day in April 2025, forex is the largest financial market in the world, and the US dollar is on one side of 89.2% of trades.
Most forex trades over the counter between banks, runs 24 hours on weekdays, and has no single central exchange.
A weaker rupee hurts importers and helps exporters. Currency moves are never good or bad for everyone.

For Indian residents, currency dealing must go through authorised banks or recognised exchanges such as NSE and BSE. Rupee-pair derivatives are only for hedging genuine exposures, and offshore leveraged forex apps are not a legal route.
